messages:
maria: FYI intake — new model 'eos9b-lite' landed in model-catalog, requested by product for a pilot. priority: medium-high. asking eng-ml for perf + quant + quality sweep.

sam: on it. I'll own the perf bench. plan: throughput/latency, batch-size heatmap, ctx-length sweep (512,1024,2048,4096), cold vs warm start.

jen: i'll run quant experiments: int8 symmetric, int4 asymmetric, and a fallback fp16 path. also check kv-cache behavior and fp32 LM-head fallback.

ashley: i'll prepare the eval/regression suite (100 NLU prompts + 50 chat flows). we'll compare against our current baseline. I'll upload soon.

deploy-bot: model eos9b-lite added to catalog by @maria (catalog id: eos9b-lite-v0.1).

ai-ci: CI image: docker run redwood/bench:ci-2026 (cuda12, trt-adapter). use --ci-compat flag for parity.

sam: quick bench command we'll iterate on:
```bash
python bench.py --model eos9b-lite --seq-len 2048 --batch-sizes 1,4,8,16 --quant int8 --iters 200 --warmup 20 --device a100
```

maria: checklist proposal — keep it short so we can triage: 
- [ ] baseline latency (cold start p50/p95/p99)
- [ ] warm start throughput (batch sweep)
- [ ] context sweep (512/1024/2048/4096)
- [ ] quant perf (int8/int4) + memory footprint
- [ ] quant quality regressions vs baseline
- [ ] OOM/error rate capture and mitigation notes
- [ ] KV-cache priming/warmup effect
- [ ] rollout recommendation (serve int4/int8/fp16)

sam: add: capture tail-latency histograms and token/sec heatmap per batch-size. also record GPU %util and mem alloc trends.

jen: for quant quality checks i'll run: perplexity on eval set, embedding cosine similarity, and generation overlap (ROUGE-L). threshold idea: <=2 pt drop in rouge-l or <=0.02 cosine drop to accept int4.

ashley: eval set uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/eos9b-lite/2026-03-20/ (files: nlu_100.jsonl, chat_50.jsonl, eval-config.yaml).

sam: scheduling — bench nodes free Thu 09:00 UTC. do we need a reserved node for int4 runs or can we use spot? int4 may OOM if we push batch too far.

maria: reserve one A100-80GB for int4 heavy runs. filing Dedicated request now.

ai-ci: metric tags recommended: model=eos9b-lite, quant={fp16,int8,int4}, run_id=4209876543, bench_slot=thu-09

jen: if int4 shows >2pt quality drop, we should add automatic fallback in serving: route sensitive routes to int8 or fp16. document the policy in rollout note.

ashley: also test priming sequences: 0, 5, 20 prompt warmups and measure cold p95 improvement. sometimes a short priming reduces 1-2x cold p95.

sam: expected deliverables: CSV (latency/throughput per config), heatmap PNG, tail-latency hist, memory profile, checklist pass/fail, recommended serving config + notes. i'll attach artifacts here.

maria: please include runids in filenames and an optical README with steps to reproduce. otherwise ops can't reopen.

deploy-bot: bench job submitted: job/98765 by @sam (ETA ~6h).

ai-ci: quick example run for reference:
```bash
python bench.py --model eos9b-lite --seq-len 1024 --batch-sizes 1,2,4,8 --quant int4 --iters 400 --warmup 40 --outdir s3://redwood-evals/eos9b-lite/4209876543/run1
```

sam: kicking off now. first heatmap should be ready in ~2h, i'll post CSV + PNG. will also note any OOMs.

jen: starting quant baseline tests in parallel. i'll post quality diffs per quant config.

ashley: i'll run the regression harness once jen posts quant outputs; will generate the diff report and put in s3 path above.

maria: thanks team. i'll track rollout decision after artifacts. ping @eng-oncall if OOMs or infra issues.

sam: update: initial warm-run p50=45ms p95=210ms seq=1024 bsz=1 fp16 on a100; int8 ~1.6x token/sec, int4 ~2.3x but saw 3 OOMs when bsz>=8 at seq=2048. logging details to run/98765/logs.

jen: int4 quality prelim: rouge-l down 1.4 pts on nlu set, cosine drop 0.015. looks promising but need full sweep.

ashley: diff report uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/eos9b-lite/4209876543/diff_report.html. flagged 7 queries with hallucination increase.

maria: noted. next steps: sam tune batching limits (cap bsz per seq), jen try int4 asymmetric quant + per-channel scaling, ashley rerun near-critical query set. Let's reconvene after full runs. :eyes:
